ratings_why.fun: Eggs hatching inside the enemy line and dormice dozing through the opening are a joy to watch grow, though the keyword load slows the first few games.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because your units fight from inside the enemy's board, and one fight-timing dial pulls three builds in different directions; no tribe today does either.

verdict_why: The core reads and plays well; the Chick's 'In the nest' wording needs one clean rewrite so players can follow who it hits and who hits it.

points.text: 'In the nest' is hard to parse: 'enemies can attack it as if it stood in your front row' swaps sides mid-sentence. Say plainly that the host's side attacks it and it counts as one of your front-row units.
Six keywords plus two counters (clock, Brood) is a lot to read at a glance; folding Brood into Egg-Painter's own text, as the risks suggest, would lighten it.
Kasimir the Peddler's lost Eggs read as 'my card did nothing'; the suggested Brood +1 on a lost Egg keeps the cuckoo fantasy and softens the feel-bad.
Sleeping-Vault Warden says 'to the right of this'; Bramble's words are 'beside'. Naming the slot rule (right in the row, nothing if empty) would read cleaner.
Coin-Turner chains two conversions (gold to Wind, Wind to hours); a line on the card showing how many ticks you'll get would make it readable at the shop.

standouts.why: Little Gernegroß is the brood parasite in one line: the enemy's biggest unit raises your Chick in its own image.
Pipit-Line Placer is a Tier 1 that teaches the whole Egg idea in five words.
Seven-Sleeper grows only if it was never needed, a lazy dormouse you can read and love at once.

weakest.why: Key-Winder is a plain dial-turner with no woodland flavour in what it does.
Day-Wage Journeyman is generic economy behind a counter you must remember from last fight.
Coin-Turner is hard to read at a glance and its coin-turning folklore barely shows.

flags.note: Copying a 100-stat golden carry, plus Brood, could swing a fight on its own.
With Gernegroß, the Midsummer Leaver can bank an enemy-sized Chick permanently on each win.
'In the nest' wording mixes up whose side and whose front row.
